cmd.despeckle.details:
Among groups of connected non-transparent pixels, those with fewer than -min pixels are made fully transparent.
With -diagonal (on by default) pixels that touch diagonally count as one group; with -diagonal=false only up/down/left/right neighbors do.
Images with nothing to erase are skipped. Note: 'ds' is the alias of downscale; despeckle is 'dsp' or 'despeckle'.

Examples:
  sprite-tools despeckle hero.png
  sprite-tools dsp sprites -r -min 8 -w -backup
  sprite-tools dsp icon.png -diagonal=false -min 2
cmd.despeckle.summary: Erase small detached specks (make them transparent)
cmd.downscale.details:
The upscale factor is detected automatically from the length of same-color runs. Use -scale to set it yourself.

Examples:
  sprite-tools downscale big.png
  sprite-tools ds -scale 4 -w
cmd.downscale.summary: Shrink an upscaled pixel art image back to 1:1
cmd.extract.details:
Colors are stored most-used first (ties in order of first appearance); fully transparent pixels are ignored and alpha is set to 255.
It fails above 256 colors, so reduce them with reduce first. The default output is <name>-palette.png.
With -save <name> the palette is also stored in the shared palette folder, so 'recolor -p <name>' can use it right away
(an existing name needs -force to be overwritten; only usable with a single file).

Examples:
  sprite-tools extract hero.png
  sprite-tools ex hero.png -save hero-colors
  sprite-tools rc -p hero-colors enemy.png
cmd.extract.summary: Extract an image's colors into a palette PNG (1 color = 1px, single row)
cmd.index.details:
Palette order is the order in which colors first appear in the image; it fails above 255 colors.

Examples:
  sprite-tools index -w
  sprite-tools ix sprites -r
cmd.index.summary: Convert to an indexed (palette) PNG with color 0 set to transparent (#ffffff00)
cmd.pack.details:
All inputs are combined in natural sort order (frame-2 before frame-10) into a single PNG.
The cell size is the largest width x the largest height; smaller images sit in the top-left of their cell (centered with -align center).
With -cols 0 the column count is the square root of the image count, rounded up. Input files cannot be overwritten, and an existing output file needs -force to be overwritten.

Examples:
  sprite-tools pack frames -o sheet.png
  sprite-tools pk frames -cols 4 -gap 1 -align center -o sheet.png
cmd.pack.summary: Combine several images into one sprite sheet (the opposite of slice)
cmd.recolor.details:
-p takes a Lospec palette name (e.g. otterisk-96) or the path of a palette PNG.
Downloaded palettes are stored in your user folder (%APPDATA%\sprite-tools\palettes) and are shared with the GUI, so they work offline.

Examples:
  sprite-tools recolor -p otterisk-96
  sprite-tools rc -p my-palette.png hero.png
  sprite-tools rc -list
cmd.recolor.summary: Remap colors to a Lospec palette (or a palette PNG)
cmd.reduce.details:
Starting with the most-used colors, each one becomes a representative and colors closer than -t are merged into it.
With -k you set a maximum color count; the weakest threshold that reaches that count or fewer is found automatically (-t is ignored).

Examples:
  sprite-tools reduce                        *.png in the current folder → *-reduced.png
  sprite-tools rd hero.png -t 0.08           merge more aggressively
  sprite-tools rd hero.png -k 16             reduce to 16 colors or fewer
  sprite-tools rd assets -r -w               overwrite everything under assets in place
cmd.reduce.summary: Merge similar colors to reduce the color count (OKLab)
cmd.slice.details:
Frames are saved as <name>-0001.png, <name>-0002.png ... Fully transparent frames are skipped.

Examples:
  sprite-tools slice sheet.png -size 32
  sprite-tools sl sheet.png -size 16x24 -o frames
cmd.slice.summary: Cut a sprite sheet into frames
cmd.trim.details:
Crops to the smallest rectangle that contains every non-transparent pixel; -pad adds transparent padding on all sides.
Fully transparent images and images that would not change are skipped.

Examples:
  sprite-tools trim icon.png
  sprite-tools tr sprites -r -pad 1 -w
cmd.upscale.details:
Pixels are enlarged as they are, without interpolation. Set the factor with -scale (default 2).

Examples:
  sprite-tools upscale hero.png -scale 4
  sprite-tools us sprites -r -scale 8 -o big
cmd.upscale.summary: Nearest-neighbor upscale by an integer factor (2-32x)

flag.align: Position of smaller images within a cell: topleft | center
flag.backup: Before overwriting with -w, copy the originals to <file folder>/%s/<run time>/ (recommended together with -w)
flag.cols: Number of columns (0 = square root of the count, rounded up)
flag.diagonal: Treat diagonally touching pixels as the same speck (use -diagonal=false to turn off)
flag.dryrun: List the target files without processing anything
flag.force_save: Overwrite even if the -save name already exists
flag.inplace: Overwrite the originals instead of writing new files
flag.max_colors: Maximum color count (0 = off; when set, the threshold is adjusted automatically to reach this count or fewer instead of -t)
flag.min_size: Erase specks with fewer pixels than this (1 or more)
flag.outdir: Folder to save results in (keeps the subfolder layout; created if missing)
flag.pack_dryrun: List the files in sheet order without writing anything
flag.pad: Transparent padding to add on all sides after trimming (px)
flag.palette: Lospec palette name or palette PNG path (e.g. otterisk-96)
flag.pattern: File name pattern when scanning folders
flag.save: Also save under this name in the shared palette folder (use with recolor -p <name>; lowercase letters, digits and '-')
flag.scale_down: Set the downscale factor manually (0 = auto-detect)
flag.slice_outdir: Folder to save frames in (default: same folder as the source)
flag.suffix: Output file suffix (may be empty when used with -o)
flag.threads: Number of worker threads (0 = number of CPU cores)
flag.threshold: Color merge distance (larger merges more, recommended 0.02-0.15)
